To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a breast cancer cell line secretes a glycoprotein of 52 kDa that is regulated by estrogen.

The 52000-MR protein secreted by the MCF-7 cells is a glycoprotein with two N-glycosylation sites, that can be deglycosylized by treatment with endoglycosydase H and that is recognized by specific monoclonal antibody.

the 52,000-Mr protein secretory product of the estrogen receptor positive MCF-7 human breast cancer cells in the presence of 17 beta-estradiol contains two N-glycosylation moieties that can be removed with endoglycosylases H and F and that the two monoclonal antibodies raised against the 52000-MR protein recognize the deglycosylates form of the molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the estrogen-regulated proteins secreted by breast tumor cells and with the study of their biological role in the development of breast cancer.
the characterization of a 52 000 Mr glycoprotein secretory product of breast cancer cells in vitro.
the study of the estrogen-regulated 52 000 Mr secreted glycoprotein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 52 500-Mr protein is a glycoprotein containing at least two high-mannose type oligosaccharide chains, which are not involved in its immunological reactivity, and which are not essential for its secretion.
the estrogen regulated 52 000 protein is a glycoprotein which is N-glycosidically linked and contains two N-glycoside chains which are of the high mannose type or hybrid in nature.
the 52 00-Mr protein is a glycoprotein which is secreted by breast tumor cell lines in culture and which is recognized by two monoclonal antibodies raised against this protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 52 500-Mr protein contains a carbohydrate moiety of approximately 2000-Da, which is not involved in the antigenic determinants of the protein.
the 52 500-Mr protein is a glycoprotein with a molecular weight of 50 500-Mr after N-deglycosylation, and that its glycosylation has no effect on its immunoreactivity.

(1) the N-glycan chains of the 52000-MR protein do not play a role in the antigenic structure of the protein; (2) they do not influence the interaction of the 5200-MR protein with its receptor; (3) they do not play a major role in its secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-gycosylated chains of the 52,000-Mr secretory protein are not essential for its immunoreactivity.
the 52 00-Mr protein contains at least one N-glycosylation site which is not essential to its biological activity.
the 52 00-Mr glycoproteins are not glycosylated in the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus.
